key: And I have said: Seek pardon of your Lord. Lo! He was ever Forgiving.
s: Noah, telling God how his people stopped their ears to his calling, recalls what he urged on them; al-Qurtubi, on 71:10 to 71:12, takes the passage as evidence that seeking forgiveness brings down rain and provision, when it comes with sincerity and leaving sin.

evidence.gloss: The third question: in this ayah and the one in Hud is evidence that by seeking forgiveness provision and rain are brought down … the manner of seeking forgiveness has already been treated in the surah Al Imran, and that it comes from sincerity and a giving up of sins; and that is the root of being answered.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Nuh 71:10, at 5428). Al-Qurtubi’s single comment on 71:10 to 71:12 has three questions; the third states in his own voice that this ayah and the one in Hud are evidence that seeking forgiveness brings down provision and rain, then cites Umar’s rain prayer and al-Hasan, and closes that the manner of istighfar (treated under Al Imran) comes from sincerity and giving up sins, the root of being answered. The sentence paraphrases exactly that, the condition included. Plain sense faithful: Noah’s complaint (71:5 to 71:9, fingers in the ears at 71:7) precedes the call to seek pardon. Evidence re-found in the packet (both ellipsis pieces). entry-check ok.
